findings.title: No security-related HTTP headers present
findings.explanation: The site does not send any of the common browser security headers (Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy). These headers tell browsers how to protect visitors from things like clickjacking, content sniffing attacks, and downgrading connections to plain HTTP. Without them the site relies entirely on other defenses to prevent common web attacks.
findings.recommendation: Add the standard security headers (at minimum Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, and a basic Content-Security-Policy) at the web server or application level.

findings.title: Session cookie missing Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite flags
findings.explanation: The PHPSESSID cookie, which identifies a visitor's logged-in session, is set without the Secure, HttpOnly, or SameSite protections. This means the session ID could be read by malicious scripts on the page (increasing the impact of any XSS) or sent over unencrypted connections, potentially letting an attacker hijack a user's session.
findings.recommendation: Configure the application/server to set the session cookie with Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite=Lax (or Strict) attributes.

findings.title: No SPF or DMARC records configured
findings.explanation: The domain has an MX record (meaning it receives email) but no SPF or DMARC records were found in DNS. Without these, it's much easier for scammers to send fake emails that appear to come from this domain, which can be used for phishing against customers or partners.
findings.recommendation: Publish an SPF record listing authorized mail senders and a DMARC record with at least a monitoring policy for this domain.

findings.title: TLS certificate expires in 60 days
findings.explanation: The site's TLS certificate is valid and currently has 60 days remaining before expiration. This is not urgent yet, but should be tracked so the site doesn't go offline or show a browser warning when it lapses.
findings.recommendation: Confirm automatic renewal is configured for the Let's Encrypt certificate, or set a reminder to renew before the expiration date.

findings.title: Server exposes outdated PHP version via X-Powered-By header
findings.explanation: The server response includes an 'X-Powered-By: PHP/7.4.3' header, which publicly reveals the exact PHP version in use. Advertising this makes it easier for attackers to target known issues in that specific version, and PHP 7.4 has been past its official support window, meaning it no longer receives security updates from the PHP project.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade PHP to a currently supported version and disable the X-Powered-By header in server/PHP configuration to avoid exposing version details.

findings.title: No IPv6 (AAAA) address configured
findings.explanation: The domain only resolves to an IPv4 address; no IPv6 address is configured. This isn't an immediate problem, but it means the site isn't reachable via IPv6-only networks, which are increasingly common.
findings.recommendation: Add an AAAA record once the hosting provider supports IPv6, to improve reachability.
